high_level_objective: Determine whether a context-graph-driven, outcome-adaptive LLM agent can design and conduct more scientifically valid long-horizon R&D than information-matched alternatives.
decision_question: What is the minimum currently identifiable and executable empirical unit for evaluating autonomous R&D?

requirements: Measures agent research behavior under at least two matched conditions.
Uses hidden or externally anchored evaluation evidence.
Requires no DeepVoice access and no unauthorized native runtime construction.
Can preserve identical model, task, feedback, target-evaluation, inference, and time budgets apart from declared treatment differences.

end_to_end_three_arm: not currently executable because full treatment is unimplemented
bundles search, graph state, evidence protocol, and held-out promotion
deterministic_protocol_mutation_only: tests validator correctness rather than autonomous research behavior

candidates.rationale: Highest thesis relevance but low identifiability and infeasible while the full treatment is unimplemented.
Separates retrieval from structured research state and is compatible with hidden-paper experimental-design tasks.
Strong direct analogue for later artifact optimization, but published costs and infrastructure make it a second-stage study.
Feasible process demonstration but lacks causal comparison and independent evaluation.
Useful prerequisite instrument test, not a sufficient autonomous-research efficacy study.

selection_rationale: SCOPE supplies direct counterevidence that naive search is not a monotonic treatment benefit.
The 2x2 design estimates the main effect of structured research state, the main effect of retrieval, and their interaction instead of bundling them.
ResearchClawBench demonstrates a public hidden-target task/rubric packaging pattern, though its final-report focus requires process metrics.
Arbor and HEP motivate explicit hypothesis/evidence state; Arbor shows structure without propagated insight is insufficient, and HEP shows self-validation must be replaced or audited.
Agent-Orchestrated Adaptive RAG supplies a direct mixed-effect retrieval-structure comparator, closing the H-B indirect-comparator gap.
Routing full reads show task-, budget-, verifier-, workflow-, and backbone-dependent effects; routing remains a separate deferred study rather than a Study A confound.

structured_research_protocol.on: stage-isolated configuration, protocol, and reporting with typed decision/evidence graph, mandatory rationale, alternatives, falsifiers, and update lineage

dynamic_retrieval.on: adaptive literature and method retrieval within the same total tool/inference budget

hypotheses.statement: Structured research state increases fatal-error-free experimental-design completion and improves low-level dataset, baseline, and metric configuration under matched budgets.
hypotheses.falsifier: No positive C10/C11 versus C00/C01 contrast, or any apparent gain disappears under condition-blind independent scoring.

hypotheses.statement: Dynamic retrieval has no assumed positive main effect; its effect may be null or negative when used without stage isolation.
hypotheses.falsifier: C01 consistently improves both high- and low-level design without raising redline errors under independent scoring.

hypotheses.statement: The structure-by-retrieval interaction is positive: retrieval contributes more when evidence acquisition is separated from protocol construction and recorded in the graph.
hypotheses.falsifier: The C11-C10 contrast is no larger than C01-C00, or added retrieval only increases citation count without changing a valid design decision.

primary_endpoint.name: fatal-error-free complete design
primary_endpoint.definition: A condition-blind plan passes all high-level main/ablation/analysis requirements and low-level dataset/baseline/metric requirements with no fabricated resource, incompatible metric, constraint violation, or post-outcome change.

secondary_endpoints: fraction of retrievals that change a hypothesis, control, resource, metric, or stopping rule
tokens, tool calls, wall time, and human intervention
selected_design.task_strategy: Use hidden-target, paper-derived dry-lab tasks through an evaluator-owned release boundary. Pilot tasks estimate variance and instrumentation failure only; pilot tasks never enter confirmation.
evaluation_strategy: Programmatic checks for resource existence, metric compatibility, required fields, and forbidden leakage where possible.
LLM rubric scoring is secondary to deterministic redlines and must be calibrated against an independent human-reviewed subset.
The root research agent never receives target papers or evaluation rubrics during treatment execution.
budget_invariants: only declared factor differences are allowed
selected_design.pilot_stop_rule: Do not launch confirmation until all four conditions complete on the predeclared pilot set, leakage tests pass, deterministic checks agree with manual review, and the evaluator yields an estimable paired variance. Two consecutive infrastructure-only failures stop the pilot for repair; they do not update H-A through H-C.
selected_design.follow_on_study: After Study A identifies a viable research-state treatment: (1) test flat queue versus tree versus tree-plus-insight with a held-out gate; (2) separately test fixed model versus calibrated query/role/depth-conditioned model–workflow routing under matched quality–cost budgets.

evidence_basis.role: direct experiment-design benchmark, search counterevidence, structured-workflow ablation
hidden-target task/rubric design and report-scoring limitations
tree/insight ablation, matched budgets, held-out admission, and scope limits
trajectory retrieval/utilization and evidence-gain stopping metrics
explicit hypothesis-evidence state and evaluator-independence requirement
unified routing formulation, common quality–cost protocol, task/budget nondominance
budget-aware resample/reroute and verifier-gated routing limits
controlled model–workflow orchestration trade-offs and difficulty counterevidence
calibrated subtask allocation, cost control, and distribution-shift limits
agent communication taxonomy and layered MCP/A2A trade-offs
human-agent collaboration grammar, authority, audit, and empirical boundary
intent-aware retrieval, semantic chunk repair, and locality limitation
compute-aware scientific retrieval and domain-reranker negative evidence
direct mixed retrieval-structure effects and cost/validity limits

dynamic_update_policy.positive: Search for replications, transfer limits, alternative mechanisms, and negative counterevidence; strengthen only the measured contrast.
dynamic_update_policy.null: Inspect power, rubric sensitivity, task heterogeneity, and whether structure helps only low-level configuration; do not declare the mechanism false.
dynamic_update_policy.negative: Search analogous cross-stage interference, graph overhead, anchoring, and utilization failures; narrow to the tested task/model/protocol.
dynamic_update_policy.execution_failure: Search implementation/specification evidence for the concrete failure; repair the same provisional node without updating scientific hypotheses.
dynamic_update_policy.retrieval_stopping: Stop a retrieval branch when new evidence does not change a hypothesis, method, control, resource, metric, or scope and independent support is sufficient.

current_blockers: Verify an evaluator-owned release boundary that excludes target papers and rubrics from treatment workspaces.
Select a pilot task subset without exposing hidden evidence to the root agent.
Provide an independent scoring route and human-calibration subset without self-attestation.
Create a separate fixed OpenResearch run contract for Study A; the current project command validates paper artifacts and cannot measure treatment outcomes.
Estimate compute/token cost before confirmation and preserve matched budgets.

feasibility_findings.finding: ResearchClawBench setup_workspace copies data and related_work but not target_study into the treatment workspace.
The pinned TaskRunner function launches a shell subprocess in the workspace with the inherited environment and does not itself create a filesystem sandbox.
feasibility_findings.implication: Prompt-level omission is not a sufficient hidden-evidence boundary; Study A needs a separate evaluator-owned filesystem or capability sandbox and a failing leakage test.

deferred_model_routing_study.question: Whether calibrated query-, role-, and recursion-depth-conditioned model–workflow routing improves the held-out quality–cost frontier without increasing fatal errors.
required_controls: same total inference and evaluation budget
logged candidate capabilities, availability, price, latency, decisions, and fallback
deferred_model_routing_study.deferral_rationale: Study A isolates structured state and retrieval with one fixed model. Routing would double the factorial and published evidence shows non-universal effects conditioned on task, budget, verifier, backbone, and workflow.

decision_changes: closed H-B direct retrieval-structure comparator gap
kept routing deferred from Study A
upgraded protocol and RAG design rationale
